Task: two additions to the erd-app crate ONLY (do not touch other crates except adding the bin target in erd-app/Cargo.toml):

1. Latency instrumentation module `erd-app/src/latency.rs` (export from lib.rs):
   - Struct `LatencyRecorder` that ingests per-frame samples: capture_ts (from frame header if present, else receive Instant), decode_ts, present_ts. Compute p50/p99/p95/max in microseconds using a simple sorted-ring or reservoir histogram (no external deps beyond std; heap allocation per push is acceptable only if lock-free cheap — prefer fixed-capacity ring buffer, performance matters).
   - `stats_json() -> String` emitting {"frames":N,"p50_us":...,"p95_us":...,"p99_us":...,"max_us":...}.
   - Unit tests: empty, single, synthetic 1000-sample distribution sanity (p50 <= p95 <= p99 <= max).

2. Headless client binary `[[bin]] name = "erd-client"` in erd-app (src/bin/erd_client.rs) for VM E2E driving:
   - clap args: --host <ip>, --tcp-port <port> (default 49152), --udp-port, --pin <8digit bootstrap PIN>, --psk-hex <64 hex> if pairing store path unavailable, --frames <N> (exit 0 after decoding N video frames), --stats-json <path> (write latency stats at end), --timeout-secs (default 30).
   - Reuse erd-app lib APIs (pairing.rs, session.rs) — read them first and wire the REAL flow: pair over signaling (PIN), TCP TLS-PSK handshake v3, UDP media receive + decode via erd-decode, count decoded frames, record latency samples per frame via LatencyRecorder, clean teardown (send BYE/close both transports), exit 0. On any failure print error to stderr and exit non-zero.
   - Keep it headless: no winit/wgpu window; decoding only, rendering optional no-op counter.

Verification (must do, include output in report): `cargo test -p erd-app` green including new latency tests, `cargo build -p erd-app --bins` success, `cargo clippy -p erd-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` zero warnings.

Work in /Users/indo/code/project/EclipticRD-Rewrite. Goal: create and actually RUN the tart VM interop E2E and latency benchmark until they PASS. Performance measurement is the absolute priority (p50/p99 frame latency, Moonlight comparison).

Environment: tart VM 'eclipticrd-ci' is running at 192.168.64.197 (macOS 15.7.7). SSH: `ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 admin@192.168.64.197` (passwordless sudo). The VM has rust toolchain? VERIFY first (`ssh ... 'which cargo || ls ~/.cargo/bin'`); if missing, install via `curl https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y --default-toolchain stable --profile minimal` over ssh.

Deliverables:
1. `scripts/vm-interop.sh` — orchestrates the real-session E2E IN THE VM ONLY (project rule: E2E never runs on the physical host):
   - rsync clients/rust workspace to VM:~/erd (exclude target dirs),
   - on VM: cargo build -p erd-host --features macos-host -p erd-app --bins (release for perf? use debug first for iteration, release for the bench run),
   - start erd-host headless on VM with --bootstrap-pin 12345678 (check erd-host/src/main.rs for exact CLI flags first — read it), plus screen-recording permission caveats: if SCK capture is permission-blocked in VM, use the host's synthetic/test capture mode if one exists (grep for test/synthetic capture in erd-host/src); document what you used,
   - run erd-client (from erd-app bin) ON THE VM against the local host: pair with PIN, handshake, decode >=10 frames, clean teardown,
   - assert INTEROP_PASS: frames >= 10, exit code 0; echo markers INTEROP_PASS/INTEROP_FAIL.
2. `scripts/bench-latency.sh` — runs the same session in release mode for >=200 frames, collects erd-client --stats-json output, prints p50/p95/p99/max to stdout and writes bench-results.json. Also write scripts/moonlight-compare.md or embed in the script: if moonlight CLI is installed locally, run an equivalent moonlight latency measurement and print a side-by-side table; if absent, print 'MOONLIGHT_BASELINE: not installed — our numbers only' and still exit 0 (our instrumentation is the deliverable; comparison runs when moonlight exists).
3. Run BOTH scripts. Iterate (fix code in clients/rust if the E2E reveals bugs — minimal fixes, note every fix) until vm-interop.sh prints INTEROP_PASS and bench-latency.sh produces bench-results.json.

Evidence to return: full paths of scripts, tail of vm-interop log showing INTEROP_PASS, bench-results.json content. Save logs to /tmp/vm-interop.log and /tmp/bench.log.

Constraints: VM-only execution for E2E/bench; do NOT modify Sources/; do NOT git commit; if erd-client is missing (R1 agent may still be writing it) WAIT by re-checking every 60s up to 30 min before failing; use only minimal diffs if you must fix Rust code.
